issues.legal_issue: An assault with a common stick causing fatal head injuries, committed without premeditation in a heat of passion, may amount to culpable homicide based on knowledge rather than murder based on intention.
material_facts: A land dispute existed between the parties, and the assault occurred while the deceased was harvesting crops.
The appellant struck the deceased on the head with a lathi during the occurrence.
The deceased suffered head contusions and a fractured parietal bone, and died in hospital the following day.
The appellant also suffered injuries in the occurrence.
The High Court found that the assault was not premeditated and occurred in a heat of passion; the appellant did not continue the assault.
issues.conclusion: The Court altered the conviction from murder to culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 Part II of the IPC. Because the appellant had already undergone the maximum sentence prescribed for that offence, it directed his release unless he was wanted in another case.
issues.legal_principle: Whether an assault with a lathi on the head shows an intention to cause death or only knowledge that death is likely depends on the circumstances, manner of assault, and nature and number of injuries considered cumulatively; a lathi is not, merely because it can be used to assault, a deadly weapon. The Court applied the distinction between intention and knowledge under Sections 302 and 304 Part II of the IPC, relying on Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab, Joseph v. State of Kerala, Chamru Budhwa v. State of Madhya Pradesh, Gurmukh Singh v. State of Haryana, and Mohd. Shakeel v. State of A.P.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_murder_conviction and common_stick_used_in_head_assault and fatal_head_injuries_followed and assault_without_premeditation_in_heat_of_passion and accused_also_injured and assault_not_continued

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_murder_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a conviction for murder.
predicates.common_stick_used_in_head_assault: The accused used a common stick to strike the victim on the head.
predicates.fatal_head_injuries_followed: The victim suffered head injuries in the assault and later died from the consequences.
predicates.assault_without_premeditation_in_heat_of: The assault arose spontaneously in a heat of passion rather than being planned beforehand.
predicates.accused_also_injured: The accused also sustained injuries during the occurrence.
predicates.assault_not_continued: The accused did not continue the assault after the head injury was inflicted.

issues.definition: When a murder-conviction appeal concerns a spontaneous, unplanned head assault with a common stick that causes fatal injuries, the accused is also injured, and the assault is not continued, the conviction is altered to knowledge-based culpable homicide.
